handbookNote: Mississippi Code Title 25, Chapter 34, "The Revised Mississippi Law on Notarial Acts," Sections 25-34-1 through 25-34-57 (RULONA-based act, effective July 1, 2021). CITATION CORRECTION (important, do not repeat the old error): Mississippi's CURRENT notary law is Chapter 34, NOT Title 25, Chapter 33 -- an earlier project note incorrectly cited Chapter 33; Chapter 34 superseded that older law when Mississippi adopted its RULONA-based act. All questions in this track cite Chapter 34 sections. Classification: APPLICATION-ONLY. Section 25-34-41(2) lists the complete qualifications for commissioning (18+ years old, US citizen or permanent resident, 30-day Mississippi residency immediately preceding application, able to read/write English, not disqualified under Section 25-34-43) -- there is no exam and no mandatory training course anywhere in the chapter, corroborated by the Secretary of State's own public notary FAQ page. Notable quirks reflected in the question set: (1) a DUAL OFFICIAL-SEAL SYSTEM under Section 25-34-33 -- individual notaries buy and hold their own personal seal at their own expense (25-34-33(1)), while SEPARATELY every county board of supervisors must supply its own "eagle" seal (inscribed "notary public" with an eagle image), held by the circuit clerk, for use by elected judges/chancellors/court clerks and Secretary of State/Assistant Secretary of State staff performing notarial acts ex officio under Section 25-34-21(1)(b)-(c); (2) a $5.00 FEE CAP under Section 25-34-9, notably low compared to most other states; (3) physical presence is still a hard statutory requirement for signing under Section 25-34-15, and while Section 25-34-39 allows notarization of electronic records (with a separate SOS registration), Mississippi has NOT adopted full two-way-audiovisual remote online notarization (RON); (4) 10 enumerated grounds for denial/revocation/suspension of a commission under Section 25-34-43(1)(a)-(j); (5) an escalating misdemeanor-to-felony penalty ladder for unauthorized-practice-of-law and 'notario publico' violations under Section 25-34-47(7)-(9) (1st offense: misdemeanor, up to $1,000 fine; 2nd offense within 5 years: misdemeanor, up to 1 year jail and/or $1,000 fine; 3rd+ offense within 5 years: FELONY, up to 5 years MDOC custody and/or $5,000 fine), including a mandatory 'notario publico' consumer-disclosure statement under Section 25-34-47(4). Content-depth rationale: 116 grounded MCQs were produced (within the ~100-140 target range) directly from the full 29-section statute text, distributed across 8 topic buckets weighted to each section's actual substantive density (commissioning/qualifications and identification/notarial-acts topics are richest; the short single-purpose sections on electronic records, and validity/rules/ESIGN, were deliberately kept to a handful of questions each rather than padded with filler or invented facts, per the site owner's 'better nothing than nonsense' rule). Pricing: $0.75 (75 cents) reflects Mississippi's tier as an application-only state with no graded exam or mandatory training course to prepare for -- consistent with this project's pricing pattern of pricing application-only/education-only notary tracks well below the $9.99 exam-state tier.
